text:
meera: Heads-up — running long-context perf suite on dedicated pool and seeing steady memory growth + jumpy tail latencies. My hunch: KV cache fragmentation + hotset churn causing more page evictions than expected.

zach: Which metrics are you looking at? any traces or profile links? :eyes:

meera: Trace + heap profile attached in the run: https://ci.internal/runs/1092 (private). Top-level observations: resident_bytes for model=redwood-7B grows ~12% over 30m for long sessions, eviction_counter_total spikes during prompt expansions. No obvious leak in runtime allocations.

kai: Can you paste the PromQL you used? would like to reproduce in grafana.

meera: Sure — rough queries I used during triage:
```
# eviction rate (counter delta per minute)
rate(kv_eviction_count_total{model=~".*7B.*"}[5m]) * 60

# resident fraction (resident kv entries / resident + paged) per model
(sum by(model) (kv_resident_entries{job="runtime"}) / sum by(model) (kv_total_entries{job="runtime"}))

# fragmentation ratio (bytes lost to fragmentation)
sum by(model) (kv_fragmented_bytes) / sum by(model) (kv_allocated_bytes)
```

sasha: Nice. Suggest adding a hotset metric: fraction of requests that hit prefetched/kv-cache entries (hot_hit_rate) and a hotset_coverage percentile: e.g., what proportion of token reads in last 10m were satisfied by top-5% resident keys. That helps distinguish small hotset churn vs broad eviction.

zach: Agreed. Two quick panels to add: 1) model-level resident_fraction heatmap over time; 2) a stacked area of eviction_rate broken down by cause (manual_compaction, lru_eviction, paged_to_disk). Also add a per-model cardinality for resident keys to avoid high-cardinality explosion.

kai: From profiler: the compaction pass wasn't triggered because the fragmentation threshold is currently 0.25 -> in these long-context sequences fragmentation slowly accumulates to ~0.28 but compaction cooldown prevents immediate run (cooldown window 10m). We saw long window of suboptimal memory layout. Lowering threshold or making compaction incremental might help.

meera: Repro steps I used: spin up dedicated-7B with context=64k tokens, warm with repeated streaming prompts, then append long synthetic dialog tokens until resident_bytes climbs. Attach small script pinned in the run. Repro is stable.

ops-bot: Note: created ticket RINF-2247 with profiling artifacts and sample run. Linked to this thread.

sasha: For alerts we should avoid noisy thresholds. Proposal: create two alerts: 1) kv_eviction_burst: if rate(kv_eviction_count_total[2m]) > 200 AND resident_fraction < 0.7 for 10m -> paged eviction storm. 2) kv_frag_growth: if increase(kv_fragmented_bytes[15m]) > 50MB and fragmentation_ratio > 0.20 for 30m -> consider background compaction.

zach: Also add a summary metric: kv_compactable_bytes (bytes eligible for compaction) and expose a gauge kv_compaction_running (0/1). That will make dashboarding +runbook triage simpler.

kai: Quick experiment idea: enable incremental compaction with rate-limit (e.g., compact 5MB/s background) and run same long-context workload. If resident growth flattens, we ship config change. I can run A/B on dedicated pool.

meera: I'll wire up the PromQL into a new dashboard draft and push to grafana as "KV cache - compactness & hotset". Leaving notes in the dashboard description about the thresholds and tradeoffs (latency vs background work).

zach: Thanks — assign RINF-2247 to kai for the compaction experiment and sasha for dashboard panels/alerts. I'll watch the A/B. :thumbsup:

meera: Thanks all. If we see regression after compaction we might need to revisit kernel/batching interactions (compaction causing CPU pressure during kernel selection). For now observability first.

ops-bot: RINF-2247 status: created -> triage_pending.
